_: The curation. One entry = one specimen page under ui-kit/specimens/.
from     which source file the block comes from (kit.html by default).
section  the kit section id; label  the block heading, verbatim.
pick     optional: show only this element (or these comma-separated siblings)
out of the block, keeping its real ancestor chain. Without it the
unwrap   drop these wrappers from that chain. Used only for a tab panel,
which is display:none until a radio outside the component is checked.
wrap     false when the block already carries .device .app-case itself.
width    the viewport the specimen is shown at. Mobile-only pieces get 360,
so the media query shows them instead of being overridden. For a
control that sits on the bare canvas the width is the measured width
of the control itself, so the frame hugs it and no strip of empty
stone is left over. For anything on a plate the width keeps the
plate's own 20px padding, because that padding is the product.
component  the page it is canonical for; also  the pages that link to it.
Sections f-color and f-type are the token foundations and are shown on
tokens.html, so they are skipped here. No em dash.

block: Text input - default / hover / focus / disabled
skip_blocks.why: That block is stand markup: .kit-field, .kit-field-wrap, .kit-field-lbl, plus .is-hover and .is-focus classes hand-written to fake the pseudo-classes. It demonstrates no product class, so it cannot be the input specimen. The field the product ships is input-amount, sliced out of the Add funds dialog.

It was the button-primary specimen until 2026-08-03, and it demonstrates .btn-primary with .btn-sm, .btn-md and .btn-lg: four classes the system declared and no painted screen ever carried. Gate 30 found them, components/button.css dropped them, and the frozen kit keeps its own copy of the nine declarations in its own <style> so this page goes on rendering as it did. A block whose whole subject has left the system cannot be a specimen of it. What the product wears is in the extra section, block 'The button family, quiet and brass'.

The same block for .btn-secondary, and it was the more expensive of the two: its rest state was identical to .auth-btn and .state-btn and its hover was not, so the one specimen a person would copy from taught a hover the product does not have. Same date, same reason, same replacement.

specimens.label: Every button the product wears
specimens.title: Every button the product wears, one row per form
specimens.note: Ten rows, one per form, and a form is a set of classes rather than a place. Two emphases times three sizes times block or not is twelve on paper; the product wears nine, and the three it does not are named with a verdict in the authored source rather than left as blank cells. The tenth row is the sign-in sheet, the only scope left in components/button.css, because it is the one row in the product that answers a pointer with a transform. No control has a plate under it: the one host that is here for the cascade gives up its surface. The column is 380, about what a sheet is in this product, so a control declaring width:100% is shown at a width it actually gets.

specimens.title: Every other control in the product that is an action

compose.kind: how it works, in the header

specimens.note: Twelve actions, none of them re-staged: each is sliced out of the specimen it already stands in, with its true ancestor chain and its siblings dropped, and every element of that chain gives up its own surface so what is left standing on the page ground is the control. The order is by how much of the product each one is, and the counts beside them are read from ui-visual at build time. Selectors and navigation are not here: a chip, a tab and a nav slot carry a value rather than a press, so their subject is the group and the selected state, and they are staged on the page of the component that owns the group.

specimens.note: The direction row out of the bet panel, which is this atom's second face. A spectator's pair states the market's two sides in green and red at rest; a trader's chooser rests on the system's quiet ground and states the CHOICE, which components/tokens.css decided when it wrote 'the tinted YES button (spectator, not trader)'. The odds figure under each label is the panel's datum and stays components/betpanel.css's, the way an event photograph is a card's content.

specimens.label: Mobile bottom nav
specimens.title: The slot face, five of them, one current
specimens.note: The bottom bar, cut where the atom stands: five slots, one of them carrying aria-current, which is the state that says where you are. What belongs to the atom is what it draws - nothing at rest but a mark, a label and an ink - and the sticky position, the ground, the groove along the top edge and the rules between the slots are the bar's and stay in components/bottomnav.css. The row face of the same atom stands on the header page, inside the account menu it drops out of.

specimens.label: The quiet chip, in both rails it ships in
specimens.title: The quiet chip, in both rails it ships in
specimens.note: One control, two containers, which is the whole point of the block. Until 2026-08-05 this chip was drawn twice, by `.cmt-controls .seg button` in comments.css and by `.ed-range button` in tabs.css, and the four painted rules were the same declaration block byte for byte. Every rule in chip.css is scoped to `.app-case` and neither ground is the chip's own, so both rails are shown whole: the sort segment stands in a --bg-well trough with a hairline, the chart range on the section.
